title: A Trip Towards Fairness: Bias and De-Biasing in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark (StereoSet) measured stereotypical bias in religious contexts by evaluating a model's preference for stereotypical sentences over anti-stereotypical sentences related to religion.
findings: All model families tested (LLaMA, OPT, BLOOM) were generally fairer (less biased) in the religion and race domains compared to the gender and profession domains. The BLOOM model family, specifically BLOOM 1.7B, was found to be particularly fair regarding religion, achieving a normalized stereotype score (nss) of 90.18, which the authors suggest is due to the careful curation of its training data.
references: Alekh Agarwal, Miroslav Dudík, and Zhiwei Steven Wu. 2019. Fair regression: Quantitative definitions and reduction-based algorithms.
